assert.rubric: The response resolves the ambiguity by asking a focused clarifying question (ideally exactly one, not a long checklist) AND offers its own recommended answer with a brief why, rather than silently assuming one interpretation of 'caching' and producing an implementation. It must NOT just start building a caching solution.

The response asks a focused clarifying question (ideally one at a time) about what 'faster' means or where the bottleneck is, and pairs that question with its own recommended answer plus a short rationale. It must NOT pick one performance interpretation on its own and dive into an implementation or code.

cases.prompt: We need authentication for the app. Set it up.

assert.rubric: Despite the 'Set it up' instruction, the response first asks a single focused clarifying question about an underspecified decision (e.g. auth method, provider, session vs token) with its own recommended default and a one-line why — instead of unilaterally choosing an auth approach and implementing it. It asks one question at a time rather than dumping a many-item questionnaire.

cases.prompt: Add an export feature to the reports page.

assert.rubric: The response surfaces the key undecided branch (e.g. export format CSV/PDF/Excel, or scope of data) by asking ONE focused clarifying question that includes a recommended answer and a brief justification, rather than assuming a format and producing implementation code for the export.
